clue.text: Marry a great deal? He's reputed to

definitions.text: Marry a great deal? He's reputed to

parts.note: to mate is to pair up or marry
a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: A question about who marries often, answered with a nod to a familiar reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: MATELOT is British slang for a sailor, who by legend has a wife in every port; so the whole clue describes him while MATE plus LOT builds him.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial seaman is said to keep a wife in every harbour, so he weds a great deal.

clue.text: Assistant who is unorthodox and firm? Yes

indicators.note: unorthodox means irregular, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Asking whether a helper is unconventional and resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' shuffles the letters of 'and firm'; the phrase recalls Crusoe's faithful servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Crusoe's servant, the phrase means a loyal general helper or right-hand man.

clue.text: Get tense hearing giant

indicators.note: hearing says we take the word as it sounds

parts.note: a titan is a giant

explanation.surface: Becoming nervous on listening to a giant.
explanation.definitionFit: To stiffen or grow taut is to become more strained.

clue.text: Priest's come round, drinks up the port

indicators.note: to come round something is to surround it

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist priest, so lama's

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks

explanation.surface: A clergyman has turned up and is drinking in the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads 'drinks' backwards in this down clue; 'come round' wraps the priest's word around that. A lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canary Islands city, it is a major Atlantic seaport.

clue.text: Heading for the pin

definitions.meaning: a ship's course or direction relative to the wind
a short nail with a broad head, a drawing pin

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sailing vessel's course and a small sharp nail.

clue.text: Second lid used to close bottle

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat, and a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: A spare cap is put on a bottle to seal it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lid' looks like the bottle's cap but is slang for a hat: a TOPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cork or bung is the plug pushed into a bottle's neck to seal it.

clue.text: Marvellous actor, a con man…

parts.note: a super is a supernumerary actor, an extra
a duper is one who dupes or tricks

explanation.surface: Praise for a performer who turns out to be a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal exclamations of delight meaning excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: …had confessed

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both possessing something and admitting a fault.

clue.text: Foolish talk beginning to perturb and irritate

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to rattle someone is to irritate them

explanation.surface: Silly chatter starts to bother and annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish chatter or babble is idle, silly talk.

clue.text: "One up," donor of cup said

indicators.note: said signals that the name is taken as it sounds

parts.note: Samuel Ryder donated golf's Ryder Cup

explanation.surface: A sponsor's remark about being ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One up' suggests winning by a hole, but means someone mounted on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseman or cyclist is a person sitting up on a mount.

clue.text: Royal drink

definitions.meaning: the title of the Ethiopian emperor, a king
a hot mixture of port or sherry, sugar and spice

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the Ethiopian sovereign's title and a warm spiced wine punch.

clue.text: Better receiving attention humbly

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
a matter in hand is being dealt with or attended to

explanation.surface: Someone improving their lot by getting noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective but is the verb CAP, to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Going about with your hat held in your hands is the picture of deference and meekness.

clue.text: The form it's'taken in sport — a league

indicators.note: taken in says one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: RU is rugby union
it, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A sporting format adopted by a league.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is the usual crossword shorthand for Rugby Union; the stray apostrophe in the print is an OCR blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony is a set form or established procedure, the prescribed order of a rite.

clue.text: Order apt to be misconstrued by hunter

indicators.note: misconstrued words are wrongly read, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction likely to be misread by a hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that preys on others is a hunter by nature.

clue.text: Responsible for term being late

parts.note: to be behind a plan is to be responsible for it
a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: Whoever set the deadline is running late.
explanation.definitionFit: Running overdue means arriving after the expected hour.

clue.text: When retreating, put in explosive stuff

indicators.note: retreating goes backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: mined means having had explosive charges laid

explanation.surface: Soldiers falling back after laying explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When retreating' turns MINED round. 'stuff' is a noun meaning fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven cloth, and this twilled cotton is a fabric.

clue.text: Quiet people wearing sort of quiet gear

indicators.note: something wearing clothes has them around it, so one piece goes inside the other
sort of suggests a version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music
men are people

explanation.surface: Silent people dressed in a hushed kind of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the second 'quiet' to EQUIT, and 'wearing' places the other pieces inside it; P is piano, quiet in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear and kit are synonyms for the tools and apparatus needed for a task.

clue.text: A book is where you'll find the crossword

definitions.meaning: a cheap edition with a soft cover
a newspaper's rear page, where puzzles are often printed

explanation.definitionFit: It means a soft-covered book and, read as two words, the rear page of a newspaper.

clue.text: Reflect on change — it may affect the staff

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of these letters

explanation.surface: Think about altering something that might affect the employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is the musical stave; 'change' rearranges REFLECT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: This C clef fixes the pitch of the lines of a musical stave.

clue.text: Bowls — take on a county team

parts.note: in cricket, to york a batsman is to bowl him with a yorker, a ball pitched at the feet
to hire is to take on an employee

explanation.surface: A bowls player joins a county side.
explanation.walkthrough: YORKSHIRE is a northern English county with a famous cricket team; 'Bowls' is the cricket verb YORKS, not the lawn game.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern English county's cricket club is a prominent first-class side.

clue.text: Delay putting money in place again

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside
in completes the instruction to place one piece inside the other

parts.note: to resite is to place again
P is penny or pence, money

explanation.surface: Postponement while cash is reinvested.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve or breathing space is a postponement or pause.

clue.text: One taken in by scheme, that's clear

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held within it

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dupe caught in a con, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One taken in' suggests someone fooled; here it is just I inside PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious or evident is easy to see.

clue.text: Fruit and eggs end up about the same

indicators.note: to end up is to turn over, so in a down clue the word reads backwards

parts.note: ova are eggs
ca is circa, about
do is ditto, the same

explanation.surface: A recipe of fruit and eggs that comes out much the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end up' turns the eggs over to give AVO; CA (circa) and DO (ditto) are standard abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: This pear-shaped green tropical produce is botanically a berry.

clue.text: Sit on the finest horse

parts.note: the best is the finest
a ride is a horse to be ridden, a mount

explanation.surface: Mounting the top horse in the stable.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle something is to sit astride it, legs either side.

clue.text: Stay firm and keep on attacking

parts.note: to be is to stay or remain
set means firm or fixed

explanation.surface: Advice to stand fast and keep up the assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass on all sides is to assail persistently.

clue.text: Some sterile dressings caused irritation

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some antiseptic bandages made the skin sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused irritation' suggests a skin rash; it means annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy or vex someone is to make them cross.

clue.text: A serviceman needs our protection

parts.note: RM is a Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A soldier needs our safeguarding.
explanation.walkthrough: RM stands for Royal Marine, a member of a British service.
explanation.definitionFit: Plate and mail are worn as defensive covering in battle.

clue.text: Thrash heartless brute

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word

parts.note: a beast is a brute

explanation.surface: Beat a cruel savage.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat or defeat someone soundly is to trounce them.

clue.text: Stuff coming back into fashion, we hear —- get the picture?

indicators.note: into says one piece is put inside another
we hear signals that the word is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: style is fashion

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to fill is to stuff

explanation.surface: Material returning to vogue; do you follow?
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns STYLE into STILE; 'coming back' gives LLIF, from FILL, which goes into it. 'get the picture?' reads as 'understand?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of fruit, flowers or other inanimate objects is a genre of picture.

clue.text: Answer provided by bible to trouble

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A response drawn from scripture to some worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Answer' looks like the letter A but is the verb meaning to serve or suffice.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer a purpose is to serve or be of use, which is to be of help.

clue.text: Lever altered into new position

indicators.note: putting letters into a new position rearranges them

explanation.surface: A lever moved to a different setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot-operated bar drives a machine such as a sewing machine or loom.

clue.text: Become airborne from strip

definitions.meaning: to leave the ground and fly
to remove clothing or a covering

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both leaving the runway in flight and removing garments.
